title: NOAA Fisheries: Green turtle
supports: Taxonomy, distribution, habitat, population status and lifespan.

title: NOAA Fisheries: Loggerhead turtle
supports: Taxonomy, distribution, habitat, regional nesting estimates and lifespan.

title: NOAA Fisheries: Leatherback turtle
supports: Taxonomy, distribution, habitat, population trends, shell characteristics and lifespan.

title: NOAA Fisheries: Hawksbill turtle
supports: Distribution, habitat, regional nesting estimates, anatomy and lifespan.

title: NOAA Fisheries: Kemp's ridley turtle
supports: Distribution, habitat, regional population information, April–July nesting, daytime arribadas and lifespan.

title: NOAA Fisheries: Olive ridley turtle
supports: Distribution, habitat, regional nesting estimates, population trends, arribada nesting and lifespan.

title: Australian Government DCCEEW: Flatback turtle
supports: Distribution, Australian breeding sites and soft-bottom habitats.

title: Queensland Government: Sea turtle nesting areas mapping
supports: Regional nesting calendars; based on Marine Turtle Breeding and Migration Atlas Project (2021). Nesting months are not migration dates.

title: Hays et al. (2000): The diving behaviour of green turtles at Ascension Island
supports: Six inter-nesting females; routine resting dive depths of 18–20 m. Surface-to-20 m band in species.json is an editorial summary.

title: Iverson et al. (2019): Loggerhead sea turtle diving changes with productivity, behavioral mode, and sea surface temperature
supports: 26 adult female tracks, northern Gulf of Mexico; approximately 80% of time at 0–30 m; study maximum 160 m.

title: Witt et al. (2011): Tracking leatherback turtles from the world's largest rookery
supports: Gabon post-nesting dispersal; predominantly surface–200 m; maximum recorded 1080 m. No coordinates extracted from figures.

title: Gaos et al. (2012): Dive behaviour of adult hawksbills in the eastern Pacific Ocean
supports: Study-specific shallow depth use, mostly within 10 m; not a universal species limit.

title: Sasso and Witzell (2006): Diving behaviour of an immature Kemp's ridley turtle from Gullivan Bay
supports: Single immature turtle; normal bottom-associated behaviour in 2–3 m water. Not a population estimate.

title: McMahon et al. (2007): Satellite tracking reveals unusual diving characteristics for the olive ridley turtle
supports: Northern Australia; individual mean maximum depths 20.1–46.7 m; recorded maximum 200 ± 20 m. Means and dive ranges are different statistics.

title: Sperling et al. (2010): Diving behaviour in two distinct populations of gravid Flatback turtles
supports: Inter-nesting TDR study: maximum 29 m at Curtis Island, 44 m at Bare Sand Island.

title: SWOT: Online Map & Sea Turtle Database
supports: Discovery source only. Nesting and telemetry records hosted at OBIS-SEAMAP; data reuse subject to SWOT terms and requests. No raw tracks downloaded.

title: OBIS: Access OBIS data
supports: Occurrence access and field definitions. Bathymetry is seabed depth, not measured turtle depth. No raw records downloaded in this session.

title: OBIS-SEAMAP: Chelonioidea species profile, CSV point-observation export (request 101809)
supports: User-provided ZIP export contains 1,835 point observations dated 2006–2020, not linked migration trajectories. The points CSV has no depth fields and no populated series IDs, so it provides neither individual tracks nor swimming-depth measurements. The archive includes per-dataset citations and reuse policies.

title: Josephson and Palka: NEFSC Aerial Circle-Back Abundance Survey 2006
supports: Four CC0 point observations labelled unidentified turtle (Chelonioidea), all dated July 2006. They are sightings, not an identified animal's track; no swimming depths are supplied.

title: Ampela and Bacon: HRC Koa Kai-11 Marine Species Monitoring Aerial Surveys November 2010
supports: 101 turtle-labelled point observations from November 2010 in the supplied profile export. CC-BY; OBIS-SEAMAP archive terms restrict redistribution without consent. Not an individual track and no depth measurements.

title: Ampela and Bacon: HRC SCC Aerial-Based Monitoring Survey February 2010
supports: 12 unidentified-turtle point observations from February 2010 in the supplied profile export. CC-BY; OBIS-SEAMAP archive terms restrict redistribution without consent. Not an individual track and no depth measurements.

title: Ampela and Bacon: HRC Koa Kai Marine Species Monitoring Vessel Surveys November 2010
supports: One unidentified-turtle point observation from November 2010 in the supplied profile export. CC-BY; OBIS-SEAMAP archive terms restrict redistribution without consent. Not an individual track and no depth measurements.

title: Pool and de Boer: SeaTurtle surveys on Braamspunt by Green Heritage Fund of Suriname
supports: 90 point observations from March 2020 in the supplied profile export: 86 turtle nests and 4 poached-nest records. CC-BY-NC; OBIS-SEAMAP archive terms restrict redistribution without consent. Nest points are not swimming locations or tracks.

title: NOAA InPort: Kemps Ridley and Loggerhead Tracking data in GOM
supports: Potential actual telemetry source for two species. Catalog inspected; files not downloaded.

title: IUCN Red List: Green Turtle (2025 assessment)
supports: Global Least Concern assessment published in 2025; assessed 9 December 2024; population trend increasing; no mature-individual count provided.

title: IUCN Red List: Loggerhead Turtle (2017 publication)
supports: Global Vulnerable assessment; assessed 23 August 2015; population trend decreasing; no mature-individual count provided.

title: IUCN Red List: Leatherback Turtle (2013 assessment)
supports: Global Vulnerable assessment; assessed 21 June 2013; population trend decreasing; no mature-individual count provided.

title: IUCN Red List: Hawksbill Turtle (2008 assessment)
supports: Global Critically Endangered assessment; assessed 30 June 2008; population trend decreasing; no mature-individual count provided.

title: IUCN Red List: Kemp's Ridley (2019 assessment)
supports: Global Critically Endangered assessment; assessed 14 January 2019; estimated 22,341 mature individuals; population trend unknown.

title: IUCN Red List: Olive Ridley (2008 assessment)
supports: Global Vulnerable assessment; assessed 30 June 2008; population trend decreasing; no mature-individual count provided.

title: IUCN Red List: Flatback (1996 assessment)
supports: Global Data Deficient assessment; assessed 1 September 1996; no mature-individual count or life-expectancy estimate provided. The assessment is old and needs updating.
